content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalties on Juniper Ridge, so this rule sits at the **preferred** position (not merely the fallback).

What I checked and why it's clean:
- **§ 1.5 (Fees definition)** — excludes service credits, interest and damages from "Fees," so no LD sneaks in through the payment obligation.
- **§ 9 (Termination)** and **§ 10 (Effect of Termination)** — contain no early-termination fee, exit charge, or minimum-fee-on-termination. § 10.2 in fact runs in our favour (Vendor refunds prepaid Fees).
- **§ 24.4** — expressly denies Vendor any right to accelerate Fees on our change of control.
- **§ 27.3** — lets us terminate for prolonged force majeure "without penalty."
- **§ 7.3** — bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due.
- Text searches for "liquidated," "penalt," "remaining," and acceleration/make-whole/forfeiture patterns surfaced nothing Customer-adverse.

Two items I considered and cleared:
- **§ 22.2 (audit shortfall)** — we pay audit costs plus the *actual* undisputed shortfall only if underpayment exceeds five percent. That is compensatory recovery of amounts genuinely owed, not a liquidated or penal sum.
- **§ 2.1 (take-or-pay, USD 2,000,000/year for three years, "without reduction or termination rights")** — this is economically penal and is a genuine problem, but it is a minimum-commitment term reviewed under the MINCOMMIT rule. Per the no-double-flagging principle, I have noted it in the rationale rather than redlining it here.

One drafting note for awareness rather than a deviation: there is no affirmative provision stating that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties. Silence achieves the preferred outcome, so no edit is warranted — but if § 2.1 is renegotiated under MINCOMMIT, that is the natural place to confirm that any agreed early-exit amount is capped at three months' Fees and is the sole liquidated amount.
